description: Intent i028 (SNAPSHOT=s07, BRANCH=error-unwind-poisoned-count) complete. Reported finding (medium confidence): snapshots/s07 drivers/md/raid5-ppl.c:976-998, quote "for (i = 0; i < le32_to_cpu(pplhdr->entries_count); i++) {\n\t\tstruct ppl_header_entry *e = &pplhdr->entries[i];\n\t\tu32 pp_size = le32_to_cpu(e->pp_size);" — Untrusted source: ppl_header.entries_count is a raw __le32 read from disk (on-disk PPL metadata) into a single 4096-byte page by ppl_load_distributed(); the only header validations are CRC, signature, and generation, none of which constrain entries_count. Violated invariant (asymmetric validation): the write/producing direction caps the count at PPL_HDR_MAX_ENTRIES (raid5-ppl.c:280-281, io->entries_count == PPL_HDR_MAX_ENTRIES, array entries[64] ends the page per include/uapi/linux/raid/md_p.h:413-428) but the read/recovery direction applies no clamp — ppl_recover() iterates the unclamped on-disk count (line 976) and indexes &pplhdr->entries[i] (line 977) past the 64-entry array for entries_count > 64, an OOB read past the 4KB page; OOB-fetched pp_size/checksum then drive the while (pp_size) sync_page_io loop (991-1005) and ppl_recover_entry() (line 784) uses pp_size/data_size as data_disks/strip_sectors loop bounds; the same unclamped count drives the offset-advance loop at 1151-1153, steering subsequent header reads to attacker-chosen disk offsets. Attacker = corrupted/tampered disk or PPL area (weaker than the seed's remote peer). Counterevidence checked: rg over drivers/md, drivers/, fs/, block/ shows no entries_count validation anywhere and no other raid consumer; seed usbip code present in s07 is PATCHED (usbip_common.c:482-485 clamps rpdu->number_of_packets, 685-693 zeroes it on error) and excluded by the seed rule; dm-era-target.c ws_inc/ws_dec loops (383/397) consume kernel-computed btree counts, classified safe. Bounded limitations: high-hit deserialization files (ocfs2, f2fs, ntfs3 fslog range_count:4565, ath12k/ath10k wmi, amdgpu_discovery, ice_ddp, idpf, bnxt, qaic_control, dm-zoned-metadata) and usb completion consumers (btusb, xhci-ring, ehci-sched, mon_bin, UVC, sound/usb) were enumerated but not deep-read; no runtime reproducer was built (read-only tree).
